notes: MACRO, on the v2 plate kit. A print, what it means mechanically, and who
`who-it-hits` is the one repeat in the vertical formats: four or five
consequences told over TIME rather than as cards in one frame. Three
cards in a 9:16 column measure 33px type, under the readability floor.

A STATIC PLATE MAY HOLD. The ceiling was written when every plate in the kit boiled; some are `playback: static` now, because a figure that moves is a figure being re-read. What keeps a data beat short is the ceiling itself (`short_max_hold_s`, 8 s), which is already more than a fifty-second cut of eight or nine beats gives any one of them.

ALTERNATE ORDERS CAME BACK WITH THE BEAT MARKERS (items 2 and 26). `sign-off-first` put the closing card ahead of the hook and stays retired: the first second is the ticker and the move. The orders below may move anchored beats, because a marked script says where each beat starts and the cut follows its markers; an unmarked script is only offered the orders that keep the beat sequence it was written to.

WIPES MARK A CHANGE OF SUBJECT (item 13): a shot with `enter: wipe` is wiped in, sweep and page alternating, at most three a short; every other cut stays hard. A wipe on every cut would be a signpost on every cut, which is none.
THE CLEAR AREA (item 27): as the stock short's, every card's words are kept inside the band a phone shows clear of YouTube's own furniture.

DENNIS ONCE (item 7). The stock and earnings shorts give him the turn in close-up; the macro short never showed him, and a CPI short with no host looked like a slideshow beside the others. `the-turn` is that same shot, on the line the cut turns on.

alts.notes: The fifth treatment: the hook on a full field with the ticker at the foot, so the eye lands on the sentence before the chip. The same slots. `hook-card-t4` is not here on purpose — it leads with the figure at 240pt, and the next beat is that figure.

What was expected over what came out, as two stacked panels. `body-1` is bound REQUIRED on purpose: the plate's caution is that without a real prior expectation it reads as a comparison against a number it invented, so the rotation only reaches for it when the script carries the consensus. The gap on the divider stays empty — it is a figure nobody wrote, and the pipeline does not compute one.

THE SERIES BEHIND THE PRINT (item 6): 27 years of it off FRED's public CSV, recessions shaded, picked from what the headline names (CPI, core CPI, PCE, unemployment, fed funds, the 10-year, GDP, oil). Preferred wherever FRED has it: one print means something only against the line it belongs to. The source line is required, so a chart nobody can check is never drawn. The KICKER IS REQUIRED TOO: the drawing runs from its title to its source line, taller than the clear band, and shrunk to fit it with the title optional the title was the line dropped, leaving a chart with no name. And NO CAPTION while it is up: the chart fills the band, so any caption sat over its years or its line.

shots.notes: The statement itself, in the band drawn for it. NO `headline-stack` ALTERNATE HERE, unlike the SHORT: the stack needs a second headline, and a required bind is a field on the writer's form — which takes MACRO to thirteen, past the dozen at which a form is a document again and gets filled in like one.
The turn, told to camera in close-up (item 7), held only while he says it (item 28). A script with no turn line drops it.
How it actually works, in the card drawn for a term and its meaning. It listens for its own first line now: the turn is Dennis's (item 7).

One consequence per beat, full size. Three in a column measure 33px type, under the readability floor, so a chain at 9:16 has to be told over time. THREE, NOT FOUR. Every step of a sequence is a field on the writer's form, and a fourth consequence took the MACRO form to thirteen — past the dozen at which a form is a document again and gets filled in like one. NEVER THE SAME CARD THREE TIMES RUNNING (item 7): each step is drawn on a layout the steps before it did not use, from the three here, `compose.plan_variants`.

alts.notes: One consequence per beat as a term and its meaning. `$n-1` steps with the sequence exactly as the authored bind does.
Design's shorts quote plate, a line a slot: the consequence is broken at the slot's 34 characters. One that needs more than its four lines leaves this plate unfillable and the rotation takes another.

meme.notes: The one place for a meme: the tail of the verdict, once both sides of it are on screen and before the close.

shots.notes: ONE THING AT STATEMENT SIZE, FIRST (item 25). The three-line close drew a conclusion in `line-1` and two empty rules under it, which is the empty furniture the samples were full of. It is an alternate now, and only for a conclusion of exactly three sentences, one a line. The handle sits in the kicker: this plate's date label is in the caption band.

alts.notes: The conclusion as a pulled line.
THREE LINES FOR THREE SENTENCES. `sent.3.i` is sentence i of a conclusion that has exactly three, and nothing otherwise, so this drawing is only in the rotation when every line has one.

orders.name: statement-first
orders.notes: What was said before what was printed: the statement straight after the hook, then the figure and the estimate. Cut only for a script whose markers put `headline` second.

orders.name: hits-before-mechanism
orders.notes: Who it hurts before why: the consequences land first and the mechanism explains them. Cut only for a script marked in this order.
